en: The Brief Recitation Method of the Bodhisattva Mārīcī,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple,
in accordance with imperial decree.
First, one should bind the seal of Vairocana Buddha.
As for the subsequent seal:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
It is accomplished by simultaneously extending both thumbs.
Recite the mantra seven times and scatter [the mudrā] over the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām* | *A-vīra hūṃ khaṃ*. Next is the mudrā for the root mantra of the Bodhisattva Mārīcī.
As for the characteristics of this mudrā:
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
extend and join the two index fingers,
and each of the two middle fingers should twist around and grasp the two index fingers so that they press against one another.
The mudrā is formed by holding both thumbs upright and joining them together.
Recite the mantra to empower five places on the body:
first the forehead, then the right shoulder, and then the left shoulder.
Next, at the heart and then above the throat,
recite each mantra once.
The mantras are as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya. Tadyathā: akāmatsi, makāmatsi, ādumatsi, jambaramatsi, mahājambaramatsi, antardhānamatsi, marīcaye matsi. Namo saptataye. Iccha iccha me. Sarvasattvānāṃ ca. Sarvatrāsāpāyebhyaḥ. Balarave vīrya svāhā.* Next, bind the heart-seal (*hṛdayamudrā*) of Bodhisattva Mārīcī.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām oṃ maricije svāhā*. Next, regarding the method for binding the heart-mantra mudrā:
Form an empty fist with the left hand;
join the index finger and the thumb together like a ring.
Visualize yourself entering into the left-hand fist.
Cover the left fist with the right hand. Then,
visualize this mudrā as the form of the Bodhisattva Marīcī,
and imagine that one's own body remains unceasingly within the heart of the Bodhisattva Marīcī.
By reciting the body-mantra, one shall immediately obtain sublime empowerment;
one will not be seen by any malevolent persons who act as obstacles,
and no calamities whatsoever shall attach to one’s person.
All disputes and verbal strife shall be extinguished.
Worms, wolves, tigers, leopards, water, fire, thieves, and bandits shall be unable to inflict harm.
Whatever worldly fruits and rewards one seeks shall all be attained in harmony.
If one cultivates supramundane dharmas,
then meditative concentration will manifest before them;
wisdom will flourish, and they will attain the power of hearing and retaining the teachings.
One should not forget the dharma of the bodhicitta.
When reciting mantras, one should deeply arouse compassion and act to uproot the suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings.
All shall attain unobstructed liberation and swiftly realize the path of unsurpassed Bodhi.
This must be kept secret and not transmitted recklessly.
*The Brief Recitation Method of the Bodhisattva Mārīcī*.
